newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian radical says his group killed union boss.
newsitem.headline: Algerian radical says his group killed union boss.

text.p: An Algerian Moslem fundamentalist said on Algerian state-run television that his guerrilla group had killed the country's top union leader, Abdelhak Benhamouda.
Moujahed Rachid, a 30-year-old university student, said one member of his seven-member group, Kamal Boulanouar, shot the union leader as part of a plan to throw the country into political crisis.

"Our programme focused on assassinations which would have great impact prompting a crisis at the level of the government. The killing of senior personalities had a significant impact", he said in a pre-recorded interview broadcast on Monday night.
Benhamouda was assassinated on January 28 outside the union heaquarters in central Algiers.
Rachid, who was once jailed for three years for holding a classified official document, said he broke away from the Armed Islamic Group (GIA) to head an "Independent and Free Group".
"We split off from the GIA because we disagree with them in the approach and in their exaggeration in killing people," he said, adding that his group comprised two cells of three and four rebels.
He emerged as the lone survivor after Algerian troops killed the other members on February 12 by firing rockets into the rebels' hideout in an apartment block in central Algiers.
The Algerian Jihad Islamic Front, a small guerrilla faction based in Algiers, has also claimed responsibility for Benhamouda's killing.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
